soft_notes.observation: Plan.md calls this 'SAVEPOINT-rolled-back' but the implementation uses `conn.begin()` (a top-level connection-scoped transaction), NOT `conn.begin_nested()` (the true SAVEPOINT API). Functionally equivalent for test isolation: the outer transaction wraps everything the service does and `trans.rollback()` reverts it all, including any Session.commit() calls (which only end the session-level subtransaction). This is the canonical pattern from the SQLAlchemy docs ('join a Session into an external transaction'). Worth flagging only so future contributors don't 'fix' this by adding begin_nested() — the current code is correct.
soft_notes.actionable_for: Optional documentation update or rename of the comment from 'SAVEPOINT' to 'rollback-only outer transaction'.

soft_notes.observation: testcontainers PostgresContainer does not expose a public attribute for stashing the engine. The plan-prescribed approach writes private attributes (`_engine`, `_url`) to pass them to db_session. Python permits this; risk is low because the testcontainers API is unlikely to evolve to use the same attribute names. Alternative would be returning a (container, engine, url) tuple from the fixture, but that breaks the existing plan contract. Acceptable as-is.
